cell_type_model: epithelium and ERBB-family receptor systems; no exact CDH1-ERBB3 model established
assay_or_perturbation: exact-pair PubMed/PMC/publisher search for E-cadherin-HER3 binding, co-immunoprecipitation, receptor phosphorylation, and perturbation; E-cadherin-EGFR evidence retained only as a family boundary
pathway_branch: E-cadherin adherens-junction branch versus NRG-ERBB3 receptor-tyrosine-kinase branch
limitations: E-cadherin-EGFR association does not establish E-cadherin-HER3 binding or activation; ERBB2/ERBB3 ligand-family and epithelial co-expression evidence were not transferred.

cell_type_model: mouse preimplantation embryos/trophectoderm; MCF-7, T47D and other breast epithelial models
assay_or_perturbation: E-cadherin/IGF1R co-immunoprecipitation and localization; CDH1 loss or knockdown; IGF1 stimulation; IGF1R/AKT phosphorylation and trophectoderm survival readouts
pathway_branch: CDH1-IGF1R contact/availability -> IGF1R-PI3K-AKT survival and epithelial adhesion branch
limitations: The interaction and receptor-facilitating role are context dependent; later CDH1-loss work found increased IGF1R ligand availability without reproducible co-IP, so a universal constitutive complex or ligand-like CDH1 activation rule is not assigned.

cell_type_model: osteoblast N-cadherin/LRP5 models and epithelial E-cadherin/Wnt contexts; no exact CDH1-LRP5 model located
assay_or_perturbation: N-cadherin-LRP5 co-immunoprecipitation and Wnt functional studies used as a paralog boundary; exact CDH1-LRP5 binding and perturbation search yielded no qualifying study
pathway_branch: E-cadherin-beta-catenin adhesion branch versus Wnt-LRP5/LRP6 signaling
limitations: N-cadherin-LRP5 association is not evidence for E-cadherin-LRP5; shared cadherin or LRP family membership and Wnt pathway co-expression were not transferred.

cell_type_model: PC12/PC9 neuronal and epithelial migration models with LAR/PTPRF and cadherin-catenin complexes
assay_or_perturbation: LAR/PTPRF co-localization and co-immunoprecipitation with beta-catenin/cadherin complexes; phosphatase and migration assays; the cited study found the association was not mediated by cadherins directly
pathway_branch: PTPRF/LAR-beta-catenin phosphatase regulation of cadherin adhesion versus direct CDH1 association
limitations: LAR/PTPRF associates with beta-catenin and cadherin-catenin complexes, but the primary evidence explicitly does not establish direct binding to E-cadherin; indirect complex context is not promoted to a molecular edge.

cell_type_model: rat lung extracts, MvLu cells, WC5 temperature-sensitive Src cells and Sf9 reconstitution models
assay_or_perturbation: PTPmu/PTPRM co-immunoprecipitation with E-cadherin; recombinant co-expression; E-cadherin cytoplasmic deletion mapping; Src-dependent dissociation and tyrosine-phosphorylation perturbation
pathway_branch: PTPRM/PTPmu -> E-cadherin-catenin tyrosine-phosphorylation control -> adherens-junction stability and cell adhesion
limitations: This is a receptor-type phosphatase/cadherin adhesion complex rather than a secreted ligand-receptor interaction; the direct association is mapped to the E-cadherin cytoplasmic region and does not imply an extracellular ligand mechanism.

cell_type_model: HT29p, MDA-MB468, Cos-7 and MCF-7 cells; transgenic mouse liver model
assay_or_perturbation: EGF stimulation; EGFR and CEACAM1 co-immunoprecipitation; EGFR inhibitor; CEACAM1 phosphorylation-defective mutant and transgenic perturbation; proliferation and Ras/MAPK readouts
pathway_branch: EGFR -> CEACAM1 tyrosine phosphorylation -> Shc sequestration/RAS-MAPK modulation -> epithelial proliferation
limitations: CEACAM1 is a membrane adhesion/inhibitory co-regulator and EGFR substrate, not an EGFR ligand; the direction and magnitude of feedback depend on CEACAM1 isoform, phosphorylation state, EGF exposure and tissue context.

cell_type_model: mouse CEACAM2 pancreatic/metabolic models and CEACAM1-EGFR epithelial comparator systems; no exact CEACAM2-EGFR model established
assay_or_perturbation: CEACAM2 expression, isoform and metabolic-function studies; CEACAM1-EGFR phosphorylation/co-IP retained as a paralog boundary; exact-pair binding and receptor perturbation search found no qualifying study
pathway_branch: CEACAM2 metabolic/adhesion branch versus CEACAM1-EGFR feedback and EGFR epithelial-growth branch
limitations: CEACAM1-EGFR evidence cannot be transferred to CEACAM2; family homology, expression and shared EGFR downstream pathways do not establish the submitted pair.

cell_type_model: activated T-cell and HEK293T CEACAM1-TIM-3/HAVCR2 models; no exact CEACAM2-TIM-3 model located
assay_or_perturbation: CEACAM1-TIM-3 cis-association, proximity ligation, co-immunoprecipitation and T-cell exhaustion studies used as a paralog boundary; exact CEACAM2-HAVCR2 search found no qualifying assay
pathway_branch: CEACAM1-TIM-3 inhibitory checkpoint branch versus CEACAM2 tissue/metabolic adhesion branch
limitations: The primary TIM-3 study establishes CEACAM1, not CEACAM2, as the cis-interacting CEACAM-family member; paralog similarity and co-expression were not used to infer CEACAM2-HAVCR2 binding or signaling.

cell_type_model: carboxyl-ester-lipase digestive/metabolic models and CXCR4 chemokine-receptor systems searched separately; no exact pair model located
assay_or_perturbation: exact-pair PubMed/PMC/publisher search for CEL-CXCR4 binding, receptor activation, chemotaxis, co-immunoprecipitation or perturbation; CEL enzymatic/metabolic and CXCL12-CXCR4 evidence kept separate
pathway_branch: CEL secreted lipase/metabolic branch versus CXCL12-CXCR4 Gi-protein chemotaxis branch
limitations: No exact CEL-CXCR4 binding or receptor-proximal relay was located; shared extracellular localization or generic chemokine and lipase pathway evidence is insufficient.

cell_type_model: Cer1/Cerberus Nodal-antagonist embryonic models and MRC2/macrophage mannose-receptor-2 matrix-remodeling models searched separately
assay_or_perturbation: exact-pair search for CER1-MRC2 binding, receptor activation, uptake, co-immunoprecipitation and perturbation; Cer1-Nodal inhibition retained only as a pathway boundary
pathway_branch: Cer1-Dan/Nodal-BMP antagonism versus MRC2 collagen/scavenger uptake and matrix-remodeling branch
limitations: Cer1 family membership, secretion and developmental expression do not establish MRC2 binding or signaling; Cer1-Nodal evidence was not transferred to MRC2.

cell_type_model: mammalian 293T/Nodal reporter systems, Xenopus embryo receptor reconstitution, and purified Cripto/Cryptic-receptor assays
assay_or_perturbation: CFC1/Cryptic or Cripto co-immunoprecipitation/cross-linking with ActRIB/ALK4; CFC-domain mutagenesis; Nodal reporter and phospho-SMAD2/3 assays; receptor-Fc SPR/SEC and domain analysis
pathway_branch: NODAL + CFC1/Cryptic -> ACVR1B/ALK4 with type-II receptor -> SMAD2/3-SMAD4/FOXH1 transcriptional complex -> developmental patterning
limitations: CFC1 is a GPI-anchored co-receptor lacking a cytosolic kinase domain; Nodal and an appropriate type-II receptor are required. Direct ACVR1B association is supported in cell-based EGF-CFC assays, while purified Cripto/ALK4 affinity is weak and context dependent.

cell_type_model: Nodal/EGF-CFC receptor-complex and embryonic patterning models; purified Cryptic/Cripto and ActRIIA receptor assays
assay_or_perturbation: Nodal receptor-complex reconstitution, CFC1/Cryptic co-receptor perturbation, SMAD reporter assays, and comparative ActRIIA-Fc binding studies; no isolated CFC1-ACVR2A binary assay validating a standalone edge
pathway_branch: NODAL + CFC1/Cryptic -> ACVR2A-containing type-II receptor complex with ACVR1B/ALK4 -> SMAD2/3-SMAD4/FOXH1
limitations: The pair is retained as a receptor-complex relay because CFC1 is required in Nodal signaling systems that use ActRIIA/B, but direct standalone CFC1-ACVR2A binding is unresolved; recent purified Cryptic/Cripto studies show weak or absent direct type-II-receptor interaction and the required ligand/receptor context must remain explicit.

cell_type_model: primary human polymorphonuclear leukocytes/neutrophils; Mac-1/CR3 adhesion models
assay_or_perturbation: factor-H-coated adhesion assays; CD11b/CD18 blocking antibodies; factor-H affinity purification and immunoprecipitation; C5a/TNF-alpha stimulation; hydrogen-peroxide activation readout
pathway_branch: CFH-GAG-tethered ligand -> ITGAM/ITGB2 Mac-1 -> neutrophil adhesion and stimulus-enhanced oxidative activation
limitations: The identified receptor is the ITGAM-ITGB2 Mac-1 heterodimer, not isolated ITGAM; factor H is an adhesion ligand and complement regulator, not a canonical cytokine ligand. The oxidative output is context dependent and no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: NKp46/NCR1 reporter cells, primary human NK cells, mouse NKp46-positive group-1 ILCs and Neisseria meningitidis infection models
assay_or_perturbation: CFP-Fc/NKp46-Fc binding; recombinant protein staining; NKp46-zeta reporter IL-2 assay; CFP silencing; Ncr1-deficient mice and properdin treatment during infection
pathway_branch: CFP -> NCR1/NKp46 -> activating-receptor signaling and group-1 ILC antibacterial response
limitations: The study establishes soluble properdin binding to NKp46 and NCR1-dependent infection protection, but the complete intracellular signaling chain and terminal TF are not resolved; complement alternative-pathway activity and NKp46 activation should remain separate layers.

cell_type_model: glycoprotein-hormone receptor systems and PAC1/ADCYAP1R1 neuroendocrine models searched separately
assay_or_perturbation: exact-pair searches for CGA-PAC1 binding, cAMP, receptor activation, co-immunoprecipitation and perturbation; FSH alpha-chain receptor structure retained only as a glycoprotein-hormone specificity boundary
pathway_branch: CGA-containing FSH/LH/CG/TSH heterodimeric hormone branch versus PACAP-PAC1/ADCYAP1R1 GPCR branch
limitations: No primary study supports CGA as a PAC1 ligand or cofactor; glycoprotein-hormone alpha-chain biology and generic cAMP signaling were not transferred to ADCYAP1R1.

cell_type_model: glycoprotein-hormone receptor and beta-2-adrenergic receptor systems searched separately
assay_or_perturbation: exact-pair search for CGA-ADRB2 binding, agonism, beta-arrestin, cAMP or receptor-complex assays; intact glycoprotein-hormone receptor structures retained as a specificity boundary
pathway_branch: CGA-containing glycoprotein-hormone receptor branch versus catecholamine-ADRB2 Gs/cAMP branch
limitations: No exact CGA-ADRB2 interaction or activation assay was located; shared GPCR/cAMP outputs do not establish direct binding.

cell_type_model: glycoprotein-hormone receptor and beta-3-adrenergic receptor systems searched separately
assay_or_perturbation: exact-pair search for CGA-ADRB3 binding, agonism, beta-arrestin, cAMP or receptor-complex assays; intact glycoprotein-hormone receptor structures retained as a specificity boundary
pathway_branch: CGA-containing glycoprotein-hormone receptor branch versus catecholamine-ADRB3 Gs/cAMP branch
limitations: No exact CGA-ADRB3 interaction or activation assay was located; receptor-family membership and shared cAMP signaling are not evidence for a CGA edge.

cell_type_model: purified human FSH-FSHR hormone-binding ectodomain complexes; recombinant gonadotropin assays and FSHR-expressing cells
assay_or_perturbation: 2.9-Angstrom FSH-FSHR structure; receptor-contact mapping and mutagenesis of the common alpha-chain; receptor-binding assays and progesterone/steroidogenic FSH bioassays
pathway_branch: CGA/FSHB intact FSH -> FSHR -> Gs/adenylyl cyclase/cAMP/PKA and steroidogenic function
limitations: CGA contacts FSHR within the intact noncovalent FSH heterodimer, but free CGA alone is not established as an FSHR agonist; receptor specificity and full signaling depend strongly on FSHB and the heterodimeric hormone conformation.

cell_type_model: orphan GPR20 expression/GPCR systems and glycoprotein-hormone receptor systems searched separately
assay_or_perturbation: exact-pair search for CGA-GPR20 binding, activation, cAMP, beta-arrestin or perturbation; no qualifying study located
pathway_branch: CGA-containing glycoprotein-hormone branch versus orphan GPR20 GPCR branch
limitations: GPR20 orphan-receptor status and generic GPCR signaling do not support CGA as a ligand; intact glycoprotein-hormone evidence was not transferred.

cell_type_model: GPR84 medium-chain fatty-acid inflammatory GPCR systems and glycoprotein-hormone receptor systems searched separately
assay_or_perturbation: exact-pair search for CGA-GPR84 binding, activation, chemotaxis, cAMP or perturbation; GPR84 fatty-acid ligand evidence retained only as a receptor-specific boundary
pathway_branch: CGA-containing glycoprotein-hormone branch versus medium-chain-fatty-acid-GPR84 inflammatory GPCR branch
limitations: No exact CGA-GPR84 interaction was located; GPR84 ligand and myeloid-function studies do not support transfer from glycoprotein-hormone pathways.

cell_type_model: LH/hCG receptor-expressing cells and purified/reconstituted gonadotropin receptor systems
assay_or_perturbation: alpha-subunit C-terminal peptide photolabeling and receptor activation; chimeric alpha/beta-hormone mapping; yoked hCG-LHR and monomeric-subunit agonism tests; cAMP readouts
pathway_branch: CGA/LHB or CGB intact LH/hCG -> LHCGR -> Gs/adenylyl cyclase/cAMP and gonadal steroidogenic branch
limitations: The alpha-chain C-terminus contributes receptor contact and activation in the intact heterodimer, but monomeric alpha-subunit was inactive in stringent yoked/reconstituted tests; no free-CGA ligand edge is assigned.

cell_type_model: PTH1R/PTH2R and glycoprotein-hormone receptor systems searched separately
assay_or_perturbation: exact-pair search for CGA-PTH1R binding, activation, cAMP, co-immunoprecipitation or perturbation; RAMP/PTH receptor complex literature retained only as a cofactor boundary
pathway_branch: PTH/PTHrP-PTH1R signaling and RAMP-modulated class-B GPCR branch versus CGA-containing glycoprotein hormones
limitations: CGA is not established as a PTH1R ligand or receptor cofactor; PTH1R-RAMP reports and shared cAMP outputs do not support a CGA-PTH1R edge.

cell_type_model: CLR-RAMP2 adrenomedullin receptor reconstitution in COS-7/HEK293 cells and amphibian receptor systems; no CGA model
assay_or_perturbation: exact-pair search for CGA-RAMP2 binding or activation; RAMP2 studies with CLR, adrenomedullin and CGRP were retained to document the precise accessory-protein boundary
pathway_branch: CLR-RAMP2/AM1 receptor-complex branch versus CGA-containing FSH/LH/CG/TSH hormone branch
limitations: RAMP2 is an accessory component of CLR/RAMP2 adrenomedullin receptor complexes; no primary evidence supports direct CGA-RAMP2 binding or CGA-dependent RAMP2 signaling.

cell_type_model: CLR-RAMP3 adrenomedullin receptor reconstitution in COS-7/HEK293 cells and amphibian receptor systems; no CGA model
assay_or_perturbation: exact-pair search for CGA-RAMP3 binding or activation; RAMP3 studies with CLR, adrenomedullin, CGRP and AM2 were retained to document the precise accessory-protein boundary
pathway_branch: CLR-RAMP3/AM2 receptor-complex branch versus CGA-containing FSH/LH/CG/TSH hormone branch
limitations: RAMP3 defines CLR peptide-receptor pharmacology with adrenomedullin-family ligands; no primary evidence supports direct CGA-RAMP3 binding or a CGA-dependent RAMP3 relay.

cell_type_model: purified/solubilized human TSH receptor and TSHR-expressing thyroid/CHO models; alpha-subunit peptide and intact TSH assays
assay_or_perturbation: TSH-receptor binding with alpha/beta subunit cross-reactivity; alpha C-terminal peptide photolabeling and cAMP induction; TSHR stimulation and downstream signaling assays
pathway_branch: CGA/TSHB intact TSH -> TSHR -> Gs/adenylyl cyclase/cAMP/PKA with context-dependent MAPK outputs
limitations: Both TSH subunits contribute to receptor binding and the alpha-chain C-terminus can affect TSHR binding/cAMP, but free CGA alone is not a validated TSHR agonist; intact TSH and receptor context are required.
